description: getPage() slices with an off-by-one end bound, returning pageSize + 1 items per page and duplicating the boundary item across adjacent pages.

required_findings.justification: items.slice(start, end + 1) is an inclusive-of-end slice where slice() itself is exclusive of its end argument — this returns pageSize + 1 elements per call, and the element at index `end` appears on both page N (as its extra trailing item) and page N + 1 (as its first item), a real, deterministic bug reproducible on any input with more than pageSize items. No external context is needed to confirm this — the arithmetic is fully visible in this one function.

optional_findings.justification: A real, independent secondary observation added after the first baseline run: getPage() never validates pageNumber >= 1 or pageSize > 0. A pageNumber of 0 or a negative value makes `start` zero or negative, and a negative start passed to Array.prototype.slice is interpreted as an offset from the END of the array rather than an error — silently returning confusing, wrong results instead of failing loudly. Distinct from req-1's off-by-one arithmetic bug (this is present even if the +1 bug were fixed), and never required, since a reviewer that focuses only on the primary off-by-one defect has still correctly solved this fixture's main point.

explanation: The canonical half-open-range mistake: slice(start, end) is already correct and exclusive of `end`; adding + 1 makes it inclusive, which is the off-by-one. Paired with correctness-02 (the same slicing idiom used correctly) so the benchmark can tell 'reviewer understands half-open ranges' apart from 'reviewer pattern-matches on the shape of slice(x, y + 1) regardless of correctness'.
